summary: MarketBeat's 8 November 2026 interview with guest Ross Given of Trader Agency argues the biggest long-term AI winners will be the companies that use AI, not those building it. Given draws parallels with railroads and the internet: the builders borrowed heavily and mostly went bankrupt, while users such as Google, Amazon and Facebook built trillion-dollar businesses on infrastructure others paid for. He says the same pattern is emerging as hyperscalers burn cash and issue debt — Google issued a 100-year bond — while compute gets cheaper. Money, he argues, is rotating from AI builders into AI users, with the S&P 500 excluding AI names rising since 1 September while AI leaders such as Broadcom, Intel, Arm, Oracle and Western Digital fell. His chosen sector is biotechnology. First pick Tempus AI (TEM), which tests cancer patients' tumours and rents its database to drugmakers; Q3 sales were about $400 million, up 23%, with new data deals worth $500-600 million, and the stock, which has ranged from $40 to $105 in a year, is about 25% off its high. Second is Recursion Pharmaceuticals (RXRX), whose AI-designed drug REC-1245 showed improvement in 87% of patients in a trial reported 2 November; it trades near $3.50-$4 with $750 million cash through 2029. Third is the iShares Biotechnology ETF (IBB), up 30% in five months, offered as lower-volatility sector exposure. Calls: TEM BUY, RXRX BUY, IBB BUY (no explicit price targets stated).
title: Why the Biggest AI Winners Won't Be the Ones Building It
